claims.statement: Under u_lambda(x,t)=lambda u(lambda x,lambda^2 t), the mixed norm L^s_t L^r_x scales by lambda^(1-2/s-3/r).
falsification_attempts: At (s,r)=(infinity,3) the exponent is zero, matching the known critical endpoint.
At (s,r)=(infinity,2) the exponent is -1/2, matching direct change of variables.

claims.statement: For each square-integrable divergence-free whole-space datum in Leray's class, there exists a global Leray-Hopf solution in L^infinity(0,infinity;L2) intersect L^2(0,infinity;dot H1).
The energy class does not reach a Ladyzhenskaya-Prodi-Serrin exponent by interpolation alone; in particular L^2_t L^6_x has index 3/2 rather than at most 1.
falsification_attempts: Substitution gives 2/2+3/6=3/2.
A concentrating Navier-Stokes rescaling preserves critical norms while decreasing the L2 norm.

claims.statement: Every Fefferman-admissible whole-space datum has a unique smooth unforced solution on a nonzero time interval.
A smooth sufficiently decaying unforced solution obeys the kinetic-energy identity and therefore has nonincreasing L2 norm throughout its smooth lifespan.
falsification_attempts: The derivation explicitly checks the convection and pressure cancellations.
Removing decay or periodic boundary conditions exposes boundary terms, so those hypotheses are retained.

claims.statement: For the whole-space solution class and hypotheses in ESS03, bounded L^infinity_t L^3_x up to T rules out a singularity at T.
A mild ancient whole-space solution whose L3 norm is uniformly bounded along a sequence t_k tending to minus infinity is identically zero.
A finite-time singularity of a whole-space mild Navier-Stokes solution generates, by record-point rescaling, a nonzero bounded ancient mild solution with a normalized nonzero value at the origin.

If a smooth whole-space mild solution has a finite endpoint T and some fixed R,delta>0 satisfy ess sup over T-delta<t<T and centers a of integral over B_R(a) of |u|^3 finite, then T is not a singular endpoint.
falsification_attempts: The rescaled fixed-time argument was attacked for moving-time convergence and global tails; fixed profile times are controlled by the local uniform ball bound, while the source-backed KNSS limit supplies mildness and nontriviality.

claims.statement: The energy inequality and Serrin-type interpolation alone imply the uniform local L3 bound M_R required by LOCAL-L3-CONTINUATION.
falsification_attempts: A self-similar concentrating scalar field with the exact energy identity has m_R in L^4/3 of time but m_R diverging pointwise as t approaches T, so energy plus Serrin interpolation cannot supply the needed L^infinity-in-time bound.

claims.statement: Finiteness of the CKN singular-set measure (zero spatial H1 measure at the first blowup time, per PR-07) alone implies the uniform local L3 bound M_R required by LOCAL-L3-CONTINUATION.
falsification_attempts: A field satisfying only the scalar energy inequality (not the full PR-07 suitable-solution hypotheses) has a single terminal singular point with zero H1 measure, yet its local L3 mass at that point diverges as t approaches T; singular-set-measure-zero geometry alone cannot supply M_R.

claims.statement: There exist R,delta>0 such that the uniform local L3 bound M_R required by LOCAL-L3-CONTINUATION holds for every smooth whole-space solution near a hypothetical finite endpoint T.
falsification_attempts: Energy plus Serrin-type interpolation alone does not supply this bound (LOCAL-L3-FROM-ENERGY, refuted).
CKN singular-set measure-zero geometry alone does not supply this bound (LOCAL-L3-FROM-CKN, refuted).

Vorticity-direction coherence, Carleman/backward-uniqueness, and Type I plus self-similar exclusion were each attacked and did not supply it either (LOCAL-L3-FROM-VORTICITY-COHERENCE, LOCAL-L3-FROM-CARLEMAN, LOCAL-L3-FROM-TYPE-I).
No known technique in this project currently derives the bound from finite-energy smooth data; a genuine proof would require new local anti-concentration structure.

claims.statement: Constantin-Fefferman vorticity-direction coherence of the KNSS record-point ancient profile supplies the local L3 bound M_R via a route independent of already invoking the full CF regularity theorem directly.
falsification_attempts: A stationary shear field has perfectly coherent vorticity direction but unbounded local L3 mass, so coherence alone does not control M_R without CF's own full finite-energy hypotheses.

If the genuine CF coherence hypothesis held for u itself, its strong-solution conclusion already implies M_R directly, making it a strictly stronger, non-modular hypothesis rather than an intermediate bridge.
A concentrating rescaled family shows CF's fixed-radius coherence length does not survive record-point rescaling, so it cannot be assumed at the profile level from KNSS compactness alone.

claims.statement: Adapting ESS's Carleman-based backward-uniqueness theorem directly to the KNSS record-point rescaled profile supplies the local L3 bound M_R from finite-energy data.
falsification_attempts: Applying backward uniqueness to the rescaled velocity directly requires a zero terminal trace, contradicting the KNSS profile's normalization |v(0,0)|=1.

Applying it to vorticity instead requires an exterior zero terminal vorticity trace not supplied by finite-energy data, and even granting that trace, a nonzero constant ancient solution has zero vorticity everywhere yet unbounded local L3 mass, so an additional decay or tail hypothesis is still required.

claims.statement: A Type I pointwise blowup rate, together with the established NRS96 self-similar L3 exclusion theorem, implies the local L3 bound M_R.
falsification_attempts: A concentrating scalar field obeying the exact Type I pointwise rate has local L3 mass over a fixed ball diverging as t approaches T, so the Type I rate alone does not bound M_R.

Applying NRS96 requires the KNSS record-point limit to be an exact self-similar profile; that implication is not established and is exactly the content of the still-blocked claim BUP-003, so invoking NRS96 here would be circular.

claims.statement: A strictly weaker hypothesis than LOCAL-L3-CONTINUATION's M_R suffices: uniform boundedness of the local L3 mass over expanding balls centered at a KNSS record-point trajectory, rather than over all spatial centers, still forces the record-point ancient profile to vanish via Albritton-Barker rigidity and rules out the finite endpoint.
falsification_attempts: The argument has not yet received an independent adversarial verification pass matching this project's proof standard, so it is recorded as conjectured rather than proved pending that review.

Finite energy still only supplies local L3 mass control in L^4/3 of time even restricted to record centers, so deriving the narrower hypothesis from finite-energy data remains exactly as open as the original M_R.

claims.statement: A mild ancient whole-space solution whose all-time centered orbit {sqrt(-t) v(sqrt(-t) dot,t): t<0} is precompact in L3 is identically zero.
falsification_attempts: Precompactness implies boundedness, and the L3 norm is invariant under centered Navier-Stokes similarity scaling.
Constant parasitic fields are not in L3; forward self-similar solutions have the opposite time orientation.

claims.statement: On the three-torus, a universal fraction of low-mode H3/2 dissipation absorbs the instantaneous nonlinear influx into every H1/2 truncation.
falsification_attempts: An exact real divergence-free high-high-to-low triad gives flux 2 A^2 while low-mode dissipation remains 2.

claims.statement: Divergence of the sum of shell enstrophies evaluated at shell-dependent times, without a synchronization or persistence hypothesis, implies H1 blowup at their limiting time.
falsification_attempts: A moving shell packet can make the diagonal series diverge while only finitely many shells are active at each fixed time.

claims.statement: On the three-torus, a fixed-width shell overlap band absorbs every nonlinear influx across a Fourier cutoff.
falsification_attempts: Flux is cubic under amplitude scaling while band dissipation is quadratic.
A high-high-to-low triad crosses an arbitrarily wide empty overlap band.

The backward-uniqueness theorem used by ESS03 requires its differential inequality, zero terminal trace, Gaussian growth control, and local parabolic L2 regularity.

claims.statement: A mild ancient solution bounded in L3 along times t_k tending to minus infinity is zero.
The Clay positive target is global and universal in the admissible initial datum.
On a periodic cube, the cited strict residual inequality certifies a true strong solution on a finite interval.
The cited residual criterion works at H1 strong-solution regularity on its smooth bounded or periodic domains with explicit viscosity dependence.
In the cited torus framework, rigorous estimators plus a scalar control inequality bound the exact solution, and a global control function gives a global solution for that datum.
Galerkin convergence and eventual passage of an a posteriori test are conditional detection results, not independent universal regularity proofs.
The cited periodic finite verification schemes for H2 and H1 balls have the report's explicit regularity assumptions and are conditional semidecision results.

Under exact Navier-Stokes scaling, the L2 norm scales by lambda^-1/2 and the homogeneous Hs norm by lambda^(s-1/2).
